summary: Next.js 15 App Router pages and routes that form the website-starter scaffold template — a ready-to-run marketing site (home, posts, about, pricing, contact) wired to Barkpark as its CMS, demonstrating real-time revalidation via webhook and form-to-CMS write via Server Actions.

intentions.title: Lower adoption friction with a zero-to-running starter
intentions.evidence: layout.tsx, page.tsx, posts/[slug]/page.tsx, about/page.tsx, pricing/page.tsx together form a complete multi-page site a new user gets via `create-barkpark-app` — no boilerplate to write, just fill in content

intentions.title: Demonstrate the full Barkpark read path in a real app
intentions.evidence: page.tsx calls getDoc + getDocs; posts/[slug]/page.tsx calls getDocBySlug and renders via PortableText — covers single-doc, list, and slug-based fetch patterns

intentions.title: Show CMS-driven write (form → Barkpark document) via Server Actions
intentions.evidence: contact/actions.ts uses defineActions + createDoc to persist a contact submission as a `contact` document — demonstrates the write path without a custom API route

intentions.title: Wire content freshness via Studio → Next.js webhook revalidation
intentions.evidence: api/barkpark/webhook/route.ts uses createWebhookHandler + revalidateBarkpark so published edits in Studio invalidate the Next.js cache automatically

intentions.title: Support a hosted demo environment without code branching
intentions.evidence: hosted-demo-banner.tsx detects barkpark.dev API URL and injects a banner warning that data resets daily — keeps demo UX honest without separate build targets
